home.title: NetPulse — Connectivity & Exit-IP Monitor for Android
home.subtitle: Continuously checks whether the open internet is reachable, shows your current exit IP and its location, and alerts you the moment the connection drops.
home.requiresAndroid: Requires Android 8.0 (API 26) or later · Free, AGPL-3.0
home.notVpnTitle: Not a VPN. It only observes.
home.notVpnDesc: NetPulse does not tunnel or intercept any traffic. It simply probes lightweight connectivity endpoints and reports the state of your existing connection — nothing is routed through it.
home.f1Desc: Probes lightweight generate_204 endpoints and treats only a strict 204 No Content as success — captive-portal and hijack pages are ignored.
home.f2Desc: Shows your current public exit IP, region, and ISP. Tap to copy. See instantly when your exit IP changes.
home.f3Desc: Distinct check / cross / ring glyphs keep the connection state readable even in the monochrome status bar.
home.f4Desc: Keeps the last N results with timestamp, outcome, latency and exit IP — and highlights the exact moment the IP changed.
home.f5Desc: Optional vibration and sound the moment connectivity drops, plus one-tap start/stop and a next-check countdown.
home.f6Desc: English and 中文 with an in-app language switch, and automatic restart on boot when monitoring was active.
home.s1Desc: One tap starts a foreground service that probes on a fixed, configurable interval.
home.s2Desc: Each check hits a generate_204 endpoint; only a strict 204 counts as a real, open connection.
home.s3Desc: The status-bar icon, exit IP and region update live, and every result lands in the check log.
home.s4Desc: If connectivity or your exit IP changes, NetPulse flags it — optionally with vibration and sound.
home.trustDesc: Runs entirely on your device with no account and no analytics. The check log stays local. To show your exit IP's location, NetPulse queries the public IP lookup service ip9.com.cn — see the Privacy Policy for details.
home.ctaTitle: Keep an eye on your connection
home.ctaDesc: Download the latest NetPulse APK and start monitoring in one tap.

privacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.intro: NetPulse is a connectivity and exit-IP monitor for Android, published by ShuttleLab. It is designed to be private: it runs on your device, has no account system, and does not collect or sell your personal data. This policy explains exactly what the app does and the one external service it contacts.
privacyPage.s1Body: All monitoring, the check log, settings, and the status-bar indicator are computed and stored locally on your device. NetPulse has no backend server of ours, no login, no advertising, and no analytics or tracking SDKs.
privacyPage.s2Intro: NetPulse makes only two kinds of outbound requests, both essential to its function:
privacyPage.s2a: Connectivity probes — it requests lightweight generate_204 endpoints to test whether the open internet is reachable. These carry no personal data beyond what any normal web request includes (your IP, as seen by the endpoint).
privacyPage.s2b: Exit-IP lookup — to display your current public exit IP, its region and ISP, NetPulse queries the third-party service ip9.com.cn (https://ip9.com.cn/get). As with any IP-geolocation lookup, that service necessarily sees the public IP address the request originates from. NetPulse sends no other data to it. ip9.com.cn is operated independently; see https://www.ip9.com.cn/ for its own terms.
privacyPage.s3Body: NetPulse requests only the permissions it needs: Internet (to run the checks), Foreground Service + Notifications (to keep monitoring and show the status icon), Receive Boot Completed (to auto-restart monitoring after a reboot, if it was active), and Vibrate (for optional disconnect alerts). It is not a VPN and requests no VPN, location, contacts, or storage permissions.
privacyPage.s4Body: We do not collect, store on our servers, transmit to ourselves, or sell any of your data. The check log and settings live only on your device and are removed when you clear them or uninstall the app.
privacyPage.s5Body: NetPulse is a general-purpose utility and is not directed at children. It collects no personal information from anyone.
privacyPage.s6Body: If this policy changes we will update this page and the date above. Questions: support@shuttlelab.org.

termsPage.title: Terms of Use
termsPage.s1Body: By installing or using NetPulse you agree to these terms. NetPulse is provided free of charge by ShuttleLab.
termsPage.s2Body: NetPulse is open-source software licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0). You may use, study, modify and redistribute it under those terms; the source is available on GitHub.
termsPage.s3Body: Use NetPulse only to monitor connections you are authorized to use. It is a passive observer — not a VPN, proxy, or traffic-interception tool.
termsPage.s4Body: NetPulse is provided "as is", without warranties of any kind. Connectivity results, latency figures, and exit-IP geolocation are best-effort and may be inaccurate; do not rely on them for safety- or security-critical decisions.
